title: Surface local persistence and action failures
description:
## Problem
Preference and archive autosaves are fire-and-forget, so localStorage or validation rejection leaves optimistic UI and success feedback without durable state. Native share or clipboard errors and slash command exceptions are also silent. Add explicit persistence and action status with retry where meaningful, while keeping expected AbortError cancellation quiet.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Make localStorage writes reject, for example through a quota or security failure.
2. Change a preference or archive item and observe optimistic UI without an error; reload restores older durable state.
3. Make clipboard sharing reject or a slash command throw and observe no user-facing failure message.
acceptance_criteria: Local preference/archive write failures are visible and recoverable; action success is not emitted before durable acceptance; share cancellation is distinguished from failure; slash command failure is announced; rejection paths have tests.
notes: Added queued preference/archive persistence status, visible failure feedback, and retry controls. Slash and share errors are surfaced rather than silently swallowed. Added queue and interaction tests.
close_reason: Implemented and verified with automated quality gates.

title: Build accessible overlay and mobile sheet foundation
description: ShareSheet and SlashMenu claim modal semantics without complete focus containment/restoration or background inertness; ShareSheet lacks Escape and scroll lock; mobile Settings visually becomes a sheet without adaptive dialog behavior or safe-area padding. Implement a shared, tested overlay foundation while preserving desktop Settings as a deliberate nonmodal popover if desired.
acceptance_criteria: Modal overlays set initial focus, contain Tab/Shift+Tab, handle Escape, restore opener focus, prevent background activation/scroll, and support safe-area insets; Slash Enter handling is scoped; mobile Settings semantics match its modality; automated interaction tests cover these behaviors.
notes: Added shared modal behavior for focus trapping/restoration, Escape, inert background, scroll lock, initial focus, and mobile safe areas; applied to Settings, ShareSheet, and SlashMenu. Added interaction tests.
close_reason: Implemented and verified with automated quality gates.

title: Make Discover save and follow states truthful
description:
## Problem
The Discover Save control is a no-op for items already structurally present in the archive, while collection follows are hard-coded component state, reset on reload, and do not affect the feed despite preview copy saying they live on the device. Define preview versus production semantics and make all labels and state behavior accurate.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Open Discover and toggle a collection Follow state.
2. Reload and observe that the hard-coded default state returns; also observe that the feed never changes with the toggle.
3. Activate Save on any Discover post and observe that only a notice changes and no archive mutation occurs.
acceptance_criteria: Save is an accurate disabled/already-saved state or performs a real durable save; Follow either persists and filters the feed or is explicitly labeled as preview; reload behavior matches the displayed promise; tests cover both controls.
notes: Discover archive state is now truthful: already-saved items are disabled and follow controls are explicitly labeled as non-durable previews with their limitations disclosed. Covered by UI tests.
close_reason: Implemented and verified with automated quality gates.

title: Prevent false collection-share success
description:
## Problem
ShareSheet allows personal/public/community submission when no valid collection exists and reports a generic success while only archiving the item. Require a valid destination, offer a create-collection path, and emit success only after the requested state is accepted.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Use an archive with no collection matching the selected personal/public/community destination.
2. Open ShareSheet and select that destination.
3. Submit while the Collection select is empty.
4. Observe the Saved to collection success despite no requested collection assignment.
acceptance_criteria: Collection destinations cannot submit without a valid collection; no success copy names a nonexistent destination; empty-state behavior is explicit; component/integration coverage includes zero-collection and valid-collection paths.
notes: Blocked nonexistent collection submissions, added a create-collection route, validated destinations, and delayed success until archive persistence completes. Covered by ShareSheet interaction tests.
close_reason: Implemented and verified with automated quality gates.

title: Validate UI/UX audit findings
description: Independently verify the reported trust, persistence, modal accessibility, responsive, and discoverability findings against the current codebase. Classify each as confirmed, partial, stale, or unsupported; identify concrete code paths and produce a prioritized implementation backlog without changing product code.
acceptance_criteria: Each critical/high finding has evidence and classification; additional material findings are recorded; implementation work is decomposed into prioritized Beads issues with dependencies where appropriate.
notes: Three independent read-only reviews completed: interaction/data correctness, accessibility/keyboard, and responsive/product UX. Confirmed: invalid collection success, Discover no-op Save, ephemeral/non-filtering Discover follows, unhandled local persistence failures, silent share/command failures, incomplete modal focus behavior, mobile Settings scroll/safe-area gaps, hidden mobile Commands trigger, landmark/skip-link gaps, undersized controls, and small essential metadata. Partial/stale: remote archive sync now exposes status/offline/retry; Archive grouping/danger treatment has improved; Reader has some view help. Runtime browser verification remains pending because no browser backend was available in this session.
close_reason: Independent reviews completed, findings classified, and confirmed work decomposed into six prioritized child issues.

title: Upgrade Next.js past published security advisories
description: npm audit reports high-severity advisories affecting pinned Next.js 16.2.10 and its bundled postcss, nanoid, and sharp dependencies. Review the installed Next 16 migration notes, upgrade to a patched stable release, and rerun all quality gates.
acceptance_criteria: Production npm audit no longer reports the identified Next.js advisory chain and tests, TypeScript, lint, and production build pass on the patched version.
close_reason: Upgraded Next.js and ESLint config to patched 16.3.4; all quality gates and production audit pass.

title: Add content snapshots, lossless export, and recovery controls
description: Implement SSRF-safe optional content capture into private Storage, snapshot manifests and retrieval, lossless JSON/archive export, revision recovery, account deletion, and user-facing account/sync/recovery/export controls.
acceptance_criteria: Users can inspect sync state, export all canonical metadata, capture/retrieve optional content privately, restore a durable revision, sign out without losing the labeled local copy, and delete cloud data intentionally.
notes: Claimed after 6j1.3. Existing schema already contains immutable revisions and private content_snapshot metadata; next implementation should add authenticated snapshot/export/recovery/delete endpoints and UI controls. Full Supabase validation remains blocked by Docker's corrupt cached Postgres layer.
close_reason: Implemented authenticated private content capture/download, lossless export, immutable revision recovery, explicit cloud deletion/sign-out retention controls, sync-state UI, recovery migration, and coverage.

title: Add local-first synced repository and first-account migration
description: Implement the ArchiveRepository-compatible client adapter, durable local operation queue, background retry/rebase, cross-tab status, and non-destructive upload/merge of existing bareaga.archive.v1 data on first sign-in.
acceptance_criteria: Edits remain instant and durable offline, resume after restart, synchronize across two clients, expose conflicts, and preserve the pre-account local archive through migration and sign-out.
close_reason: Implemented durable local-first synced repository, rebase/retry queue, cross-tab local persistence, conflict retention, and first-account merge migration.

title: Implement authenticated archive APIs and transaction store
description: Add Supabase server clients and authenticated GET /api/archive plus POST /api/archive/sync. Apply validated batches atomically with ownership checks, operation idempotency, revision history, response limits, and no-store caching.
acceptance_criteria: Authenticated users can initialize, fetch, and synchronize an owned archive; replayed operations are idempotent; unauthorized access and malformed batches are rejected; transaction behavior is integration-tested.
notes: Implemented Supabase SSR claim verification, authenticated no-store archive GET/sync routes, a bounded validated API contract, service-role store with retry/idempotency, and locked compare-and-swap Postgres RPCs. 74 Node tests, TypeScript, lint, build, and direct PostgreSQL 16 migration/atomicity/idempotency/RLS assertions pass. Full Supabase container smoke test is tracked in 6j1.5 because the host had 964 MiB free and Docker containerd failed image pulls with an I/O error.
close_reason: Authenticated archive API and atomic durable transaction store implemented and validated; full Supabase service-stack smoke test is separately tracked as environment follow-up 6j1.5.

title: Define synced archive architecture and synchronization contract
description: Choose optional account/auth and durable storage infrastructure; specify versioned archive and content snapshot schemas; implement and test the local-first operation/rebase contract before API or UI work.
acceptance_criteria: Architecture decision is documented, Postgres/RLS schema is executable, sync payloads are runtime-validated, and deterministic conflict/rebase behavior is covered by tests.
close_reason: Defined and documented auth/storage decisions, added executable Supabase schema and RLS policies, and implemented a runtime-validated sync v1 reference reducer with deterministic conflict tests.

title: Partition current product work into a clear commit history
description: Audit the full dirty worktree and create multiple capability-focused commits with descriptive messages so future agents can understand the product and development progression from git history.
acceptance_criteria: All intended worktree changes are assigned to coherent commits; commit messages explain product intent and technical scope; Beads state aligns with completed work; quality gates pass; final git status and commit log are reported.
close_reason: Partitioned the validated product worktree into capability-focused commits with descriptive subjects and bodies; tests, lint, TypeScript, and production build pass.

title: Simplify product IA and About page
description: Rename and reorganize the primary product surfaces: move the source catalog to Sources, refocus Discover on shared collections/articles/links, rename Product to About, and simplify the About page to describe Reader, Sources, Discover, and Archive with a smaller hero and fewer grids.
acceptance_criteria: Primary navigation uses Reader, Sources, Discover, Archive, and About; source catalog is available under Sources; Discover presents shared collections/articles/links; About page uses a compact hero and simple section-based functionality overview; legacy route behavior is handled intentionally; tests, typecheck, lint, and build are checked.
close_reason: Completed navigation reorganization, compact About page, Sources/Discover separation, legacy redirects, documentation updates, and full validation.

title: Redesign archive library experience
description: Critically improve the archived links and articles UI so the library has stronger editorial hierarchy, clearer navigation and item states, better action prioritization, accessible controls, and robust responsive behavior while preserving archive features.
design: Keep Bareaga's warm editorial visual language, but reduce form-like chrome and establish a calm two-pane library with expressive saved-item cards.
acceptance_criteria: Archive page has a purposeful library header, scannable collection navigation, clear search/filter/sort controls, refined article cards with progressive disclosure for secondary actions, accessible focus/labels, and usable mobile layout. Lint, tests, and build pass.
notes: Rebuilt archive hierarchy and interactions: collection-aware masthead and stats, shelf navigation, contextual filter counts, search clear, three sort modes, prioritized article typography, visible personal notes, progressive disclosure for organization/export, accessible labels/focus targets, and responsive layouts. npm test (62/62), lint, and production build pass. In-app browser was unavailable for screenshot QA.
close_reason: Implemented and validated archive library redesign

title: Fix Maximum update depth loop on app load
description: Starting the Next.js dev server and loading the app repeatedly emits React's 'Maximum update depth exceeded' browser error. Investigate the client state/effect loop in the current UI worktree and prevent repeated state updates on initial render.
acceptance_criteria: Loading /, /discover, and /settings does not emit Maximum update depth errors, and existing interaction behavior remains intact.
close_reason: Stopped the Reader slash-context effect from retriggering Chrome state every render. Stabilized empty feed/custom-source arrays and refresh identity in useFeedQuery; slash context now bails out on unchanged data and only clears on unmount.

title: Make slash command palette + / button global (part of design-system grounding)
description: The slash menu and its / button were reader-only, breaking header parity across pages. Added ChromeProvider (global slash/settings open-state + a slot the Reader registers feed-specific commands into). SiteHeader now renders the / button, Settings button, SlashMenu and SettingsPanel on every page; global , / // ⌘K keyboard handling moved there. slashCommands.ts: reader-only groups (Topics, Articles, refresh/search actions) gated behind an optional reader context; new Navigate group (Go to Reader/Discover/Archive/Social/Product) shown on every page. NewsApp registers its reader context via effect and keeps only r/? shortcuts. Build + lint pass; verified slash menu opens on Reader (with Topics/Articles) and Discover/Archive (reduced) and , opens Settings via keyboard.
close_reason: Implemented and verified in browser

title: Wire custom sources through /api/feeds validation and ranking
description: feedContract.ts:parseFeedQuery hard-rejects any source id not in catalogSourceIds(), and feeds.ts builds its sourceById map only from SOURCE_CATALOG. Both need to also recognize a requesting user's custom sources (resolved from prefs) so /api/feeds doesn't 400 on a legitimately-added custom source, and ranking.ts/getSource() attribution (name, homeUrl) resolves correctly for them.
design: Depends on the data-model task for where custom sources are read from, and on the SSRF-hardening task since this is the code path that actually triggers the network fetch.
acceptance_criteria: Requesting /api/feeds with a custom source id the user has added succeeds and returns articles; requesting an arbitrary unknown id (not in catalog, not a real added custom source) is still rejected exactly as today.
close_reason: Implemented add-source-by-URL UI (Discover + Settings > Sources) backed by a new SSRF-hardened /api/sources/preview endpoint, and wired custom sources through /api/feeds via a new POST path (parseFeedBody, createFeedPostHandler) that re-validates client-supplied sources server-side and never publicly caches.

title: Harden server-side feed fetch against SSRF for user-supplied URLs
description: Today every feedUrl fetched by feeds.ts (parser.parseURL) is a value the project authors hardcoded into sources.ts, so the fetch target is fully trusted. Bring-your-own-feeds means the server will fetch a URL a visitor pastes in, which is a new SSRF risk (e.g. a URL pointing at 169.254.169.254, localhost, or an internal service, including via redirect). Add validation before any fetch of a user-supplied feed URL: enforce https, resolve and reject private/link-local/loopback/multicast IP ranges, re-check the target after following redirects (not just the initial URL), and keep the existing timeout/size caps.
design: This is the one piece of this epic that is a genuine new attack surface, not a UI/data-model extension of existing trusted behavior — treat it as security-critical, not a nice-to-have validation pass.
acceptance_criteria: Attempting to add a source whose feed URL resolves (directly or via redirect) to a private/loopback/link-local address is rejected with a clear error and never reaches parser.parseURL; a normal https Substack/blog feed URL still works.
close_reason: Implemented HTTPS/DNS SSRF validation, redirect revalidation, timeout, and response-size limits.

title: Add custom-source data model and prefs persistence
description: UserPrefs.sourceOrder (src/lib/types.ts) currently only stores IDs that must already exist in the hardcoded SOURCE_CATALOG (src/lib/sources.ts). There is no way to persist a user-supplied feed. Add a customSources: SourceDef[] (or minimal subset: id, name, feedUrl, homeUrl, plus defaulted editorial fields) field to UserPrefs, wire it through prefs.ts load/save/migration, and merge it with SOURCE_CATALOG wherever sources are resolved by id (getSource(), sourceById maps in feeds.ts and ranking.ts).
acceptance_criteria: A custom source added via prefs survives reload, appears in getSource()/sourceById lookups everywhere the catalog is queried, and existing prefs files without the new field still load correctly (backward-compatible migration).
close_reason: Implemented custom source persistence, normalization, ordering, and merged source lookups.

title: Bring-your-own-feeds: import Substack and custom RSS/Atom sources
description: Bareaga's PRD lists bring-your-own-feeds as the immediate roadmap item (docs/PRD.md 'Now' row): let a user paste any RSS/Atom URL (Substack newsletters, personal blogs, any CMS feed) into the existing source manager rather than being limited to the 51 hardcoded catalog sources. The fetch/cache/rank/archive pipeline (src/lib/feeds.ts, ranking.ts) is already source-agnostic RSS/Atom via rss-parser and handles per-source failure isolation; the missing pieces are entirely upstream: no data model for a user-added source, /api/feeds hard-rejects any source id outside the static catalog (src/lib/feedContract.ts), no feed-URL discovery UX, and no SSRF-safe handling for fetching a URL a visitor supplies (today all feedUrls are trusted, hardcoded values).
design: Reuses the existing generic RSS/Atom pipeline (feeds.ts, rss-parser) rather than building a new fetcher. Custom sources get a minimal SourceDef with sensible defaults for the editorial-only fields (sourceType, cadence, depth, defaultRank) so Discover's filters don't break on missing metadata.
acceptance_criteria: A user can paste a Substack (or other blog) URL into Discover or Settings > Sources, Bareaga resolves it to a working RSS/Atom feed (via Substack's /feed convention or HTML <link rel=alternate> autodiscovery), the source appears alongside catalog sources in every existing view (Grid/Top/Focus/Ranked, Archive, Social) with correct name/attribution, persists across reloads via prefs, and the server-side fetch of the user-supplied URL is hardened against SSRF (blocks private/link-local IP ranges and redirects to them, enforces https, caps size/timeout).
close_reason: Completed custom source persistence, SSRF-safe discovery and fetching, private feed API transport, and source management UI with regression coverage.

title: Ground the design system: shared shell across all pages
description: Reader, Discover, Archive, Social, and Product each hand-roll their own header, hero, footer, and button vocabulary in a dedicated stylesheet, with numeric drift (4 wordmark scales, 4 header rhythms, 3 near-duplicate hero blocks, 2 button languages, 2 content widths, missing footers). Extract shared primitives (SiteHeader, PrimaryNav unification, PageHero, SiteFooter, AppShell), add spacing/type/width scale tokens to base.css, put global appearance Settings on every page, unify content width to 1480px, and delete the now-dead per-page CSS.
notes: Done. New shared primitives: AppShell, SiteHeader (wordmark + section label + unified PrimaryNav + global Settings + tools slot + subline), PageHero, SiteFooter. Added layout/spacing/type scale tokens to base.css + new shell.css. PrimaryNav collapsed to one rendering (readerStyle removed); all pages show all links with aria-current underline; Archive count badge shows app-wide. Settings (theme/palette/font/density) now reachable on every page, opens to Appearance tab on non-reader pages. Cross-cutting chrome via window 'bareaga:chrome' CustomEvent (, shortcut + slash-menu 'open settings'). Product moved onto shared header + 1480px width (dropped 1240px + double-padding), kept its editorial hero/feature-grid/manifesto/CTA-footer, added .product-subnav. Deleted dead per-page CSS from reader/discover/archive-social/product/responsive. Build + lint pass. Verified all 5 pages + Settings-on-archive in browser.
close_reason: Closed

title: Create shared app shell and browser data stores
description: Centralize theme hydration, shared navigation, preference state, and archive state behind reusable providers/hooks and repository interfaces. Separate archive domain operations, seeded demo fixtures, validation/migrations, and localStorage implementation so synced storage can replace persistence without rewriting screens.
acceptance_criteria: Reader, Discover, Archive, and Social use one theme/prefs integration; archive mutations go through a typed repository with runtime validation and migration tests; page shells share navigation primitives; the existing synced archive feature can depend on the repository rather than UI-local storage functions.
close_reason: Centralized preference/theme and archive state in root providers; introduced typed archive repository, localStorage adapter, fixtures, domain operations, runtime validation and migrations; moved Reader, Discover, Archive, Social, and ShareSheet off direct persistence; added shared primary navigation and migration/repository tests. 30 tests, TypeScript, lint aside from tracked font warning, and build pass.

title: Harden feed API and isolate server-only modules
description: Define a validated feed-query contract, deduplicate and reject unknown inputs, protect or rate-limit force refresh before deployment, make cache semantics explicit, and split server-only RSS/provider enrichment from browser-safe engagement formatting with server-only guards.
acceptance_criteria: The public route validates and deduplicates ids/topics, abusive refresh requests cannot repeatedly fan out to publishers, server-only code cannot enter client module graphs, and route/cache behavior has automated tests.
close_reason: Validated and deduplicated feed query contract; rejected unknown inputs; added bounded per-client forced-refresh budget; made cache headers explicit; isolated RSS/provider code with server-only guards; added route, cache, validation, and limiter tests. Tests, TypeScript, lint, and build pass.

title: Extract and harden reader feed orchestration
description: Move feed request/cache/abort/progressive-refresh state out of NewsApp into a focused query hook or service with an explicit state model. Preserve cached sources during revalidation, use bounded parallel batches or justify sequential behavior, tolerate per-batch failures, and reduce NewsApp to composition and user intents.
acceptance_criteria: Cached sources do not disappear during background refresh; batch failures do not prevent unrelated sources from loading; cancellation, topic changes, retry, and force refresh have automated coverage; NewsApp no longer owns transport/cache mechanics.
close_reason: Extracted reader transport/cache/cancellation into useFeedQuery and a bounded-concurrency feed orchestrator; preserved cached sources during revalidation; isolated batch failures; added cancellation, topic, retry, force-refresh, merge, and concurrency tests. Tests, TypeScript, production build, and lint (aside from the existing font warning) verified.

title: Preserve removed sources during preference merge
description: The legacy merge path appends every starter source to sourceOrder, which undoes Discover removals after reload. Treat an explicitly stored sourceOrder, including an empty array, as the user's enabled set while still defaulting when the property is absent.
acceptance_criteria: Removing starter sources or all sources persists after LocalPrefsStore reload; missing sourceOrder still receives the starter defaults.
close_reason: Updated preference merging to preserve explicit enabled-source sets, including empty sets, added regression coverage, and verified removal persistence across a live reload.

title: Build Discover Sources MVP
description: Split the built-in source catalog from the default enabled set, enrich source metadata with topics and tags, add a /discover browsing and search experience, and let users locally add or remove catalog sources while preserving the current starter set.
acceptance_criteria: A dedicated Discover nav/page supports search, category and metadata filters, source preview cards, and persistent add/remove actions. Existing users retain the current starter sources by default. Tests, lint, typecheck, and build pass.
close_reason: Implemented the local-first Discover Sources MVP with a 51-feed catalog, preserved starter set, discovery filters and sorting, persistent add/remove and private ratings, responsive UI, and regression coverage.

title: Add Obsidian and Notion archive interoperability
description: Make Bareaga archives portable into existing knowledge systems through open Markdown with frontmatter, CSV, copyable citation/clip formats, and documented import affordances; preserve source URL, authorship, notes, tags, collection, and timestamps.
acceptance_criteria: Users can export an archive or collection to Obsidian-friendly Markdown and Notion-friendly CSV/Markdown without losing URLs, notes, tags, collection context, or saved dates.
close_reason: Implemented Obsidian-friendly Markdown with frontmatter, Notion-friendly CSV, per-item copyable Markdown, archive/collection export controls, and export preservation tests.

title: Add synced archival storage and durable snapshots
description: Move the local-first archive behind a synced storage interface so saves, notes, tags, and collections travel across devices; add optional content snapshots and export/import while preserving canonical URLs and source context.
design: Optional Supabase passwordless auth; Postgres immutable archive revisions and idempotent operations; private Storage for captured content; same-origin Next.js authenticated APIs; sync v1 uses server revisions and field-level optimistic conflict detection, with explicit server-wins conflicts for same-field and delete/update races.
acceptance_criteria: Authenticated archives sync across devices, save metadata remains portable, and users can export their data without losing canonical source context.
notes: Foundation slice completed in bareaga_web-6j1.1. Remaining implementation is sequenced as 6j1.2 authenticated APIs, 6j1.3 local-first client sync/migration, then 6j1.4 snapshots/export/recovery/account controls. Keep parent open until cross-device acceptance criteria pass.
close_reason: All subtasks (6j1.1-6j1.5) complete. Cross-device authenticated sync, portable metadata, and lossless export are implemented and validated end-to-end: pgTAP passes, and a live smoke test against the running Supabase stack confirmed real Auth signup, PostgREST RLS scoping across archives/archive_revisions/content_snapshots, and private Storage bucket access control all behave correctly.

title: Build archive, collections, and archive search experience
description: Expand Bareaga beyond RSS reading with a first archival product slice: saved-item states, collections, archive-native search/filtering, and a credible shared/social collection concept that fits the existing editorial UI.
acceptance_criteria: Users can navigate to an Archive surface, search and filter saved material, change meaningful archival states, create collections, and see how collections can be shared; state persists locally and the existing reader still builds.
close_reason: Implemented reader-to-archive saving, persistent archive states, notes, search, filters, collections, collection creation and sharing intent; build and tests pass.

title: Implement reader UX hierarchy and mobile ergonomics
description: Apply the attached UX audit to the Bareaga reader and product surfaces, prioritizing truthful loading state, entity decoding, mobile progressive disclosure, clearer reading modes, settings hierarchy, story scanability, and accessibility.
acceptance_criteria: Reader reports configured/loaded/failed sources accurately; encoded feed titles render correctly; mobile toolbar exposes stories sooner; reading modes are explained; settings and story hierarchy are improved; product page is rebalanced; relevant checks pass.
close_reason: Implemented the UX audit priorities: truthful progressive status, entity decoding, mobile progressive disclosure, mode explanations, settings tabs and source search, story hierarchy/accessibility improvements, return bar, and a shorter product page. Lint and production build pass.

title: Add transparent personalized article ranking
description: Implement a Ranked home view with weighted keyword rules, per-source preferences, recency and normalized engagement scoring, diversity adjustments, visible score explanations, keyword highlighting, persisted settings controls, and automated tests.
close_reason: Implemented transparent personalized ranking, persisted keyword/source preferences, UI controls, score explanations, highlighting, diversity, tests, and production/browser verification.

title: Restore Grid as a third reading view
description: Bring back the original source-column Grid alongside Top and Focus, preserving column controls, drag reordering, source-level errors, and per-source retry without regressing the new accessibility and transition guarantees.
acceptance_criteria: Grid, Top, and Focus are all selectable with accessible selected-state semantics; legacy Grid preferences remain Grid; Grid supports configured columns, drag reordering, source details, and retry; lint and build pass.
close_reason: Restored Grid as a first-class third view with original column controls, drag ordering, detail options, and source retry; lint and production build pass.

title: Rework feed views and accessibility contracts
description: Implement the requested Settings accessibility behavior, transition consistency, selected-state semantics and touch targets, recency-based Focus, deterministic balanced Top, clearer loading/import/feed errors, and simpler keyboard/settings UI.
acceptance_criteria: Settings has a truthful accessible interaction contract; topic label/content cannot disagree; selections expose semantics with adequate targets; Focus is globally recency-sorted with Compact/Detailed modes; Top is deterministic and transparently balanced; loading and errors are human-readable; keyboard help and Settings are simplified; quality gates pass.
close_reason: Implemented and verified; lint has no errors and the production build passes.

title: Remove Sources index utility row
description: Remove the Browse sources and All sources utility strip so category groups begin immediately at the top. Preserve a way to reset the category filter by toggling the active selection off.
acceptance_criteria: No utility strip appears above categories; categories remain accessible; clicking an active category resets filtering to all sources; tests and lint pass.
close_reason: Removed the Sources utility strip and added active-category toggle-off behavior; all tests, lint, and production build pass.

title: Compact Sources category index
description: Remove the oversized Sources hero, eliminate the boxed grid treatment between category groups, and move a substantially tighter category index to the top of the page while preserving category filtering and an All sources reset.
acceptance_criteria: Sources has no large hero treatment; categories appear near the top; category groups have no dividing grid borders; broad and narrow filters remain accessible and functional; tests, lint, and build pass.
close_reason: Removed the Sources hero, converted category navigation to a compact borderless index at the top of the page, retained accessible filtering/reset behavior, and passed all quality gates.

title: Replace Sources hero with category hub
description: Redesign the Sources tab hero as a responsive, grouped category navigation hub inspired by the supplied sketch. Category links must drive the existing directory filter and replace the horizontal category scroller.
acceptance_criteria: Sources hero presents grouped primary categories and nested subcategories; choosing any category filters the directory; selected state is visible and accessible; layout works on desktop and mobile; lint/tests/build pass.
close_reason: Implemented responsive Sources category hub, connected broad and narrow category filters, added accessible selected states, and verified with full tests, lint, TypeScript, and production build.

title: Expand curated source collection for culture, arts, and history
description: Substantially broaden the built-in source catalog, emphasizing high-quality culture, arts, museums, literature, criticism, archives, and history sources while preserving existing source contracts and UI behavior.
acceptance_criteria: The curated catalog is substantially larger; culture, arts, and history are prominently represented; source metadata remains valid; relevant tests and build pass.
notes: Expanded SOURCE_CATALOG from 51 to 111 sources. Added first-class culture, arts, and history topics with 22, 30, and 14 sources respectively; expanded discovery facets; verified all 66 themed feeds parse with rss-parser; npm test, npm run lint, and npm run build pass.
close_reason: Implemented and validated expanded culture, arts, and history source directory

title: Progressively disclose Reader and Sources complexity
description: Reader actions and ranking reasons compete with headlines, while Sources exposes four advanced filters and a long category rail before results on mobile. Existing view help is partly tooltip-only. Add touch-accessible explanations and progressive disclosure while preserving the editorial visual system.
acceptance_criteria: Reader view behavior is explained without hover-only UI; ranked reasons and repeated story actions use accessible progressive disclosure; mobile Sources can reach results before advanced filters; sort terms are explained; RSS configured uses user-facing language.
notes: Added contextual story actions, progressive ranking explanations, Reader view guidance, mobile advanced-filter disclosure, and clearer source/feed terminology.
close_reason: Implemented and verified with automated quality gates.

title: Improve mobile discoverability and semantic navigation
description: The only visible Slash Menu trigger is hidden on mobile; skip navigation is absent; some routes nest main landmarks; external new-tab behavior is inconsistently announced; frequent controls and essential metadata fall below the product's size conventions. Address these targeted issues without broad visual redesign.
acceptance_criteria: Mobile exposes a visible Commands/Shortcuts action; every route has one unnested main and a skip target; new-tab links have consistent accessible text; priority touch controls meet the 44px convention; essential metadata uses at least the agreed readable floor.
notes: Added skip navigation, corrected main landmarks, mobile Commands access, external-link announcements, safe-area support, and larger priority tap targets.
close_reason: Implemented and verified with automated quality gates.

title: Run destination sync suite against live GitHub/Notion sandbox and full Supabase stack
description: Mirrors 6j1.5. Full npm test / tsc --noEmit / npm run lint / npm run build / supabase test db, plus a manual smoke checklist: real GitHub PAT + scratch repo push, real Notion OAuth sandbox connect + page create/update, forced 401 surfaces 'Reconnect Notion' without a silent retry loop, disconnect+reconnect the same destination creates no duplicate pages/files.

title: Add DestinationsPanel UI: connect, status, failure inspection, disconnect
description: src/components/DestinationsPanel.tsx mounted as its own <details> section in src/components/ArchiveApp.tsx after the existing 'Sync, recovery & account' block (~line 412), following the already-extracted PublishPanel pattern (~line 402). title: Validate publish/discover flow against live Supabase stack
description: Run the full publish -> public page -> RSS -> follow -> discover flow against a running local Supabase stack (supabase start / db reset) the way 6j1.5 validated sync. Confirm anon/unauthenticated reads only see published public/unlisted material, owner-only writes are enforced, and pgTAP RLS tests pass.
design: Check df -h before assuming a Docker/disk problem, per prior session note about tight local disk space.
acceptance_criteria: npm run test:db passes for the new tables' RLS policies; a live smoke test confirms an unauthenticated client can read a published collection and its RSS feed but not private archive data.
notes: Disk was at 8.3GB free (97% used, tighter than the ~16GB the prior session flagged) -- pruned 12.66GB of reclaimable/unused Docker images (0 active containers, 0 active images at the time) with explicit user approval before starting Supabase, per the session's disk-tightness note. supabase start -> supabase db reset applied all four migrations cleanly, including this epic's two new ones (20260904140000_collection_publications.sql, 20260904150000_collection_follows.sql) with zero errors -- confirms the schema/RLS/RPC SQL is syntactically and semantically valid, not just plausible-looking. New supabase/tests/collection_publications.test.sql (21 pgTAP tests, all passing alongside the existing 12 in archive_sync.test.sql = 33/33) covers: publish_collection creates a row+items, republish keeps the original slug even when a different one is requested and replaces items wholesale, unpublish_collection sets unpublished_at, RLS lets a non-owner read a live public/unlisted publication but not an unpublished one (while the owner still can), the collection_follows RLS policy allows self-follow/self-unfollow but rejects following on someone else's behalf (42501), and authenticated clients cannot call publish_collection/unpublish_collection directly (service-role only, 42501). Additionally ran a live smoke test (temporary script, deleted after -- not committed) exercising the actual production SupabaseCollectionPublicationStore class end-to-end against the live stack with two real auth.admin.createUser() accounts: publish -> republish (slug stability, visibility update) -> getBySlug -> list (owner's own) -> listPublic (discovery, correct itemCount) -> follow -> listFollowed -> unfollow -> unpublish (drops out of both getBySlug and listPublic). Explicitly asserted no ArchiveItem.note field appears on any published item. All passed. npm test 102/102, tsc, lint clean throughout. Stopped the Supabase stack afterward (disk pressure); .env.local with local dev keys was left in place (gitignored) for future sessions' convenience. bareaga_web-5bv (parent epic) is now fully validated end-to-end and ready to close.
close_reason: Live-validated against a real local Supabase stack: all four migrations (including the epic's two new ones) applied cleanly via db reset; 33/33 pgTAP tests pass (21 new, covering publish/republish/unpublish RPCs and RLS for collection_publications/collection_publication_items/collection_follows); a live smoke test of the actual production store class confirmed the full publish->discover->follow->unpublish lifecycle and that no private archive field leaks onto a published item.

title: Add follows and public collection discovery
description: Authenticated follow/unfollow of a published collection (collection_follows table, RLS scoped to follower_id = auth.uid()), and a discovery listing surface for public (not unlisted) collections with pagination, wired for a later connection to Explore.
design: Unlisted collections stay reachable only via direct slug link and are excluded from discovery listing at the query level.
acceptance_criteria: A signed-in user can follow and unfollow a public collection; a discovery page lists public collections without exposing unlisted or private ones; follow state persists across devices via the synced auth session.
notes: supabase/migrations/20260904150000_collection_follows.sql: collection_follows(publication_id, follower_id) with a single 'for all' RLS policy -- USING scopes select/update/delete to follower_id = auth.uid(), WITH CHECK additionally requires the target publication be live (unpublished_at is null, visibility in public/unlisted) so a follow can't be created against a withdrawn/private row. No RPC needed (unlike publish/unpublish): a follow only ever references a publication row, so authenticated users manage their own rows directly under RLS, same pattern as the archives table's owner-insert policy. Store: SupabaseCollectionPublicationStore gained PublicCollectionReader.listPublic() (visibility='public' only, per the design note -- unlisted stays link-only and never appears in discovery; offset/limit pagination fetches one extra row to compute hasMore, then a separate items count query grouped in JS rather than relying on untested PostgREST embedded-relationship count syntax) and CollectionFollowStore (follow/unfollow/listFollowed, preserving most-recently-followed order). API: /api/collections/discover (unauthenticated, public cache headers), /follow, /unfollow, /followed (authenticated). UI: new /c (discovery index, offset-paginated) and a FollowButton client component wired into /c/[slug] -- note there is no sign-in UI anywhere in this codebase yet (only signout/delete assume an existing session), so FollowButton surfaces the 401 as 'sign in to your Bareaga account' text rather than linking a sign-in flow that doesn't exist. ArchiveApp's Publish panel now links to /c. Did not touch /discover (DiscoverApp/SocialApp) or PrimaryNav -- the bead explicitly frames connecting this to Explore as later work, not part of 5bv. Verification: npm test (102/102), tsc --noEmit, lint, build all clean, all new routes present in the build's route table. NOT verified: live Supabase (RLS policy execution, actual follow persistence) -- same constraint as 5bv.1-5bv.3, deferred to 5bv.5.
close_reason: Follows (collection_follows table + RLS) and a public-collection discovery listing (/c index + /api/collections/discover, scoped to visibility=public only) are implemented, with follow/unfollow wired into a new FollowButton on /c/[slug]. 102/102 tests, tsc, lint, and build all clean. Live Supabase verification deferred to 5bv.5, the last remaining subtask of bareaga_web-5bv.

title: Add public collection pages and RSS output
description: Unauthenticated, stable public URL (e.g. /c/[slug]) rendering a published collection's items, curator notes, and attribution using either RLS-scoped public reads or an admin client with explicit visibility filtering. Add an RSS 2.0 feed endpoint per published collection for update tracking.
design: No client-side direct PostgREST access from the browser; server-rendered page + route handler use the admin client with explicit visibility filtering, matching the rest of the codebase's server API pattern. RLS stays as defense-in-depth.
acceptance_criteria: A public/unlisted collection is viewable at its stable URL by an unauthenticated visitor; private archive material is never exposed; an RSS feed is available and validates against the collection's published items.
notes: src/lib/collectionPublicationStore.server.ts: SupabaseCollectionPublicationStore now also implements PublicCollectionReader.getBySlug(slug) -- an unauthenticated read using the admin client with EXPLICIT visibility/unpublished filtering (not relying on the collection_publications RLS policy as the enforcement point, since the admin client bypasses RLS entirely; RLS stays defense-in-depth for a hypothetical future direct client read), per the design note on the bead. src/lib/collectionPublicationRss.ts: dependency-free RSS 2.0 generator (renderCollectionRss) with XML escaping and a self-referencing atom:link; deliberately omits per-item pubDate since derivePublicationSnapshot() (5bv.1) never carries the private savedAt an item pubDate would need -- 5 unit tests cover escaping, ordering by position, and structure. src/app/c/[slug]/page.tsx: unauthenticated server-rendered public collection page (React cache() dedupes the generateMetadata + page reads of the same slug within one request); src/app/c/[slug]/rss.xml/route.ts: the feed endpoint. Both intentionally do NOT catch-and-404 on a thrown error from the store -- only a genuine null (not found/unpublished/private) becomes a 404; a real backend error (e.g. Supabase outage) is left to fall through to Next's default error handling, so a misconfigured deployment surfaces as a 500 rather than silently reading as 'every collection link is broken.' New src/styles/public-collection.css registered in globals.css, reusing existing design tokens (no new page-level CSS system). Verification: npm test (99/99), tsc --noEmit, lint, and build all clean, including the new dynamic routes appearing in the build's route table. NOT verified: an actual browser hit against a live page -- this repo has no .env.local and the local Supabase stack is stopped, so createAdminSupabaseClient() would throw immediately regardless of route code; a real end-to-end check needs the live stack from 5bv.5 (which needs approval to start).
close_reason: Public /c/[slug] page and /c/[slug]/rss.xml feed implemented on top of the 5bv.1/5bv.2 contract and store, with explicit (non-RLS-reliant) visibility filtering for the unauthenticated admin-client read path. 99/99 tests, tsc, lint, and build all clean. Live browser/Supabase verification deferred to 5bv.5 (no .env.local or running local stack in this environment).

title: Define collection publication architecture and contract
description: Design how a private, JSON-embedded archive collection becomes a stable, publicly-readable object without exposing private archive material. Specify normalized Postgres tables (collection_publications, collection_publication_items, collection_follows) separate from the private archives/archive_revisions tables, RLS policies for public/unlisted reads and service-role-only writes, slug generation/uniqueness, and a TS domain module that derives a public-safe publication snapshot (title, description, curator note, attribution, per-item title/url/source/excerpt/curator comment) from a private ArchiveCollection + its items, explicitly excluding private fields (personal note, tags, state, starred, topic).
design: Mirror the 6j1.1 pattern: schema + RLS as SQL migration, runtime-validated TS contract, deterministic unit tests before any API/UI work.
acceptance_criteria: Executable Postgres migration with RLS/RPC exists; a TS module can derive a validated public-safe publication payload from private archive data with unit tests covering slug uniqueness and field exclusion; design documented in bead notes/design.
notes: Schema: supabase/migrations/20260904140000_collection_publications.sql adds collection_publications + collection_publication_items, normalized and separate from archives/archive_revisions (which stay owner-only). RLS: anon+authenticated may SELECT any row where unpublished_at is null and visibility in (public,unlisted); owners can additionally SELECT their own drafts/unpublished rows via archives.owner_id join. All writes go through two SECURITY DEFINER RPCs (service_role only, revoked from anon/authenticated), mirroring initialize_archive/commit_archive_sync: publish_collection() (upsert keyed on (archive_id, collection_local_id); slug is assigned once and never changes on republish; items are replaced wholesale each publish) and unpublish_collection() (soft-delete via unpublished_at). Discovery (public vs unlisted) is a query-level filter on top of RLS, not a separate policy. TS contract: src/lib/collectionPublication.ts defines CollectionPublicationSnapshot/Item types, proposeSlug/slugWithSuffix (retry-on-collision is the caller's job in 5bv.2), derivePublicationSnapshot(collection, items, options) which explicitly excludes item.note/tags/state/starred/topic/savedAt/articleId (per-item curatorComment is only ever supplied explicitly, never defaulted from the private note), and parsePublicationSnapshot() for runtime validation of the wire payload, mirroring archiveSync.ts's parse* pattern. 12 unit tests in collectionPublication.test.mjs cover slug validity, item ordering/filtering, the private-field exclusion guarantee, and payload validation edge cases. npm test (89/89), npx tsc --noEmit, npm run lint, and npm run build all pass. Migration was NOT applied against a live Supabase instance this session (stack was stopped; starting/resetting it needs explicit approval per session instructions) — reviewed carefully against the syntax/RLS conventions already proven working in 20260904120000_synced_archives.sql. Live RLS verification is 5bv.5's job; 5bv.2 can now build the authenticated publish/unpublish/update API routes and store on top of this contract.
close_reason: Publication schema, RLS, service-role RPCs, and a runtime-validated TS domain contract are implemented and unit-tested (89/89 tests, tsc, lint, build all clean). Live Supabase RLS verification deferred to 5bv.5 pending approval to start the local stack.

title: Maximum update depth exceeded loop in Reader slash-command registration
description: During dcu.4 (add-source-by-URL UI) manual testing, dev logging showed a repeated 'Maximum update depth exceeded' React warning. Root cause: the effect in NewsApp.tsx that registers Reader commands into ChromeProvider's readerSlash state (via setReaderSlash) previously returned a cleanup that cleared readerSlash to null on every dependency-array change, not just on unmount. Since currentSources (from useFeedQuery) and other deps change frequently, this null-then-set cycle on every re-run drove repeated context updates and looped the render tree.
design: Fix already present in the current (uncommitted) working tree at src/components/NewsApp.tsx:139-179: (1) the registration effect now bails out via a functional setReaderSlash update that returns the previous object unchanged when topic/search/sources/busy are unchanged, avoiding redundant state updates; (2) the null-clearing cleanup was moved to its own effect with dependency array [setReaderSlash] only (a stable setState setter), so it fires solely on unmount instead of on every dependency change. This is the standard fix for this class of React loop.
acceptance_criteria: Exercise AddSourceForm and Reader topic/search/refresh flows in a real browser with devtools open; confirm no 'Maximum update depth exceeded' warning appears in the console across topic switches, search typing, and refresh.
notes: Dev server terminal logs (2026-09-04) show clean, successful /archive, /, and /api/feeds requests with no crash/error during a session that exercised these flows — consistent with the fix holding, though terminal HTTP logs do not capture browser-console React warnings, so this is not itself conclusive. Filing so dcu.4 does not close with this regression untracked.
close_reason: Live-verified fixed in browser (2026-09-04): loaded /, exercised topic switching, search typing, force refresh; loaded /discover, added a live Substack source (heathercoxrichardson.substack.com) via AddSourceForm, confirmed it rendered in Reader alongside catalog sources (22/23 sources, 185 stories), then removed it. Read browser console via read_console_messages with an unfiltered pattern across the whole sequence -- only [HMR] connected logs appeared, zero React warnings/errors, no 'Maximum update depth exceeded'. Confirms the code fix documented at NewsApp.tsx:139-179 (bailout comparison + unmount-only cleanup effect) holds under the exact flows that originally surfaced the bug.

title: Feed URL discovery: Substack convention + HTML autodiscovery
description: Users will paste a publication URL (e.g. a Substack homepage or a blog's homepage), not a raw feed URL. Resolve a pasted URL to an actual RSS/Atom feed: try the Substack '/feed' convention first, then fall back to fetching the page HTML and parsing <link rel=alternate type=application/rss+xml|application/atom+xml> autodiscovery tags (covers WordPress, Ghost, and most static-site blogs). If a feed URL is pasted directly, use it as-is. Must build on the SSRF-safe fetch from the sibling hardening task.
design: Two-tier resolution: (1) known-convention guess (Substack /feed) tried first since it avoids an extra HTML fetch, (2) generic autodiscovery via HTML <link> tag as fallback.
acceptance_criteria: Pasting a Substack publication URL, a WordPress/Ghost blog homepage, or a direct feed URL all resolve to a working feed; an unresolvable URL produces a clear error rather than a silent failure.
close_reason: Implemented direct-feed passthrough, native Substack /feed resolution, HTML RSS/Atom autodiscovery, SSRF-safe candidate fetching, clear failures, and regression coverage; verified against a live Substack homepage.

title: Add live Obsidian and Notion sync adapters
description: Build optional authenticated adapters after archive sync exists: write Markdown notes into an Obsidian-compatible vault workflow and upsert archive records into a chosen Notion database while keeping Bareaga's open export formats authoritative and avoiding lock-in.
acceptance_criteria: Users can configure an optional destination, sync new or changed archive items with stable IDs, inspect failures, and disconnect without losing Bareaga or exported data.
notes: Architecture decided 2026-09-04: Obsidian via a GitHub git-repo bridge (server pushes Markdown via Contents/Tree API using a user PAT; user syncs the repo into their vault with any Obsidian git plugin). Notion via full OAuth (public integration, hosted consent screen); Notion refresh-token behavior is flaky in practice so a 401 must flip the destination to a first-class 'auth_error'/reconnect state, never a silent retry. Push is automatic after each /api/archive/sync commit (via after()) plus a Vercel Cron catch-up/retry worker, driven off archiveSync.ts's existing entityVersions revision tracking rather than a second diff pass. Secrets encrypted in Node (AES-256-GCM) at rest, never in Postgres. Full design in /Users/dylanchidambaram/.claude/plans/sparkling-kindling-wigderson.md. Sequenced as 2u2.1 (schema/contracts) -> 2u2.2 (Obsidian/GitHub, first vertical slice) and 2u2.3 (Notion OAuth) in parallel -> 2u2.4 (UI) -> 2u2.5 (live suite), mirroring 6j1's phasing.

acceptance_criteria: A user can publish a collection at a stable URL, control its visibility, follow updates, and discover public collections without exposing private archive material.
notes: Implemented the local product layer: sourced social clips, share sheet destinations, public/community collection types, follows, manual URL/snippet publishing, and an explicit local-preview boundary. Stable public URLs, real identities, community permissions, and cross-user feeds still require synced storage.
close_reason: All five subtasks (5bv.1-5bv.5) complete. Collections can be published at a stable, owner-controlled-visibility URL (/c/[slug]) with curator notes and attribution, discovered via a public listing (/c) that excludes unlisted/private collections, followed/unfollowed by signed-in users, and read as RSS. Schema, RLS, and RPCs are validated against a live local Supabase stack (33/33 pgTAP tests, plus an end-to-end store-level smoke test with real Auth accounts). Connecting this to the existing Explore/Discover surface is intentionally left as future work per the bead's own framing.

title: Add archiveRecoveryApi handler test coverage
description: archiveRecoveryApi.ts (export/revisions/restore/capture/download/account-delete handlers from bareaga_web-6j1.4) has zero test coverage, unlike archiveApi.ts (archiveApi.test.mjs) and collectionPublicationApi.ts (collectionPublicationApi.test.mjs added in bareaga_web-5bv). Add archiveRecoveryApi.test.mjs with a fake in-memory ArchiveRecoveryStore, mirroring the established pattern. Separately, desugar SupabaseArchiveRecoveryStore's parameter-property constructor to match archiveSyncStore.server.ts's convention, for consistency (not currently a live blocker since archiveRecoveryApi.ts checks errors by message string rather than instanceof, so no value import from the server-only-guarded file is needed for handler tests).
acceptance_criteria: archiveRecoveryApi.test.mjs exists and passes, covering auth checks and the success/error status-code paths for each handler; npm test, tsc --noEmit, lint, and build remain clean.
notes: archiveRecoveryApi.test.mjs added, 6 tests, all passing, no blocker hit: unlike collectionPublicationApi.ts, archiveRecoveryApi.ts maps store errors by message string comparison (e.g. cause.message === 'Revision not found') rather than instanceof a custom Error class, so the fake MemoryArchiveRecoveryStore never needed a value import from the server-only-guarded archiveRecoveryStore.server.ts -- only ArchiveRecoveryStore's type shape matters, which a plain JS fake object satisfies structurally without any import at all. Also desugared SupabaseArchiveRecoveryStore's parameter-property constructor to match archiveSyncStore.server.ts's convention, for consistency (this specific fix wasn't required for the new test to pass, but removes the same latent trap for any future test that does need a value import from that file). 121/121 unit tests, tsc, lint, and build all clean.
close_reason: Added archiveRecoveryApi.test.mjs (6 tests covering all six handlers' auth/validation/status-code paths) and desugared SupabaseArchiveRecoveryStore's constructor for consistency with archiveSyncStore.server.ts. 121/121 tests, tsc, lint, build all clean.
